fatal_errors: The proposed Nb doping intervention is unrelated to the target intervention of liquid-metal dealloying a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu.
The initial material is incorrectly treated as a conventional defective W–Cu composite rather than an as-cast single-BCC WTaVTi alloy with W/Ta-rich dendrites and sacrificial Ti/V-rich channels.

The cited evidence concerns NbC formation in a laser-cladded CoCrFeNi–WC coating and provides no evidence that Nb forms a stabilizing interphase, suppresses voids, or improves thermal conductivity in W–Cu.
The hypothesized Nb-rich or NbC-like interphase lacks a carbon source and has no established thermodynamic or kinetic basis under the proposed W–Cu processing conditions.
The response omits the target selective Ti–Cu exchange, retention of RHEA ligaments, and spontaneous W-rich passivating interlayer.
Processing and service conditions are not quantified and do not match the reported 1200 °C, 96 h liquid-metal-dealloying treatment, temperature-dependent thermal testing, or 25 keV He+ screening.
It conflates thermal-conductivity behavior of the finished composite with irradiation evidence, whereas irradiation was performed only on precursor dendrites as a proxy for the RHEA ligaments.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad W–Cu joining context and proposes a comparative control experiment, but it does not reconstruct the material, intervention, mechanism, conditions, or measured outcomes of the target study. Its central Nb-interphase claim is speculative and is supported only by an unrelated laser-cladded HEA/WC coating study. The experiment could test the proposed alternative at a basic level, but irradiation dose, species, temperature, thermal-conductivity direction, Nb concentration, and statistical criteria are unspecified. Consequently, it is neither an evidence-supported alternative nor a partial reconstruction.
